The main takeaway from our work is that

the FP is not a flat surface, and the FP coefficients depend not only on the global cluster properties, but also on the distribution of the properties of galaxies in a given sample, and this should be taken into account when comparing samples of different clusters and/or redshifts.
the fundamental plane is not universal, but rather a bent surface, and its shape is strongly dependent on the distribution of galaxy properties in the particular data sample under analysis.

, in order to study the evolution of ETGs in a cosmological context, it is necessary to take into account their distribution in the FP, as well as the distribution of their photometric/kinematics properties, and to compare data at different redshift from samples with similar distributions of these properties.
